'''Glennys Reynolds Farrar''' (born 1946) is an American physicist. She is a professor of physics at [[New York University]] who specializes in [[particle physics]], [[cosmology]] and the study of [[dark matter]].<ref>{{Google Scholar id|_agEI5IAAAAJ}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last1=Cartwright|first1=Jon|title=Hunt for fifth force focuses on Bullet Cluster|url=http://physicsworld.com/cws/article/news/2007/may/09/hunt-for-fifth-force-focuses-on-bullet-cluster|access-date=2019-04-28|work=[[Physics World]]|date=2007-05-09}}</ref> She has made several significant contributions to the fields of [[hadron]] and dark matter phenomenology, helping to develop the working "Standard Cosmological Model".<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Brodsky |first1=Stanley J. |last2=Farrar |first2=Glennys R.|author1-link=Stanley Brodsky |date=1973-10-29 |title=Scaling Laws at Large Transverse Momentum |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.31.1153 |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=31 |issue=18 |pages=1153–1156 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.31.1153|bibcode=1973PhRvL..31.1153B }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Farrar |first1=Glennys R. |last2=Peebles |first2=P. J. E.|author2-link=Jim Peebles |date=2004-03-20 |title=Interacting Dark Matter and Dark Energy |journal=The Astrophysical Journal |volume=604 |issue=1 |pages=1–11 |doi=10.1086/381728 |arxiv=astro-ph/0307316 |bibcode=2004ApJ...604....1F |s2cid=20046388 |issn=0004-637X}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Profile: Glennys Farrar |url=http://projects.nyujournalism.org/tellingstories/profile-glennys-farrar/ |access-date=2022-04-22 |website=Telling Stories |language=en-US |archive-date=2022-01-26 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220126013911/http://projects.nyujournalism.org/tellingstories/profile-glennys-farrar/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Farrar is a figure in developing many modern particle-search techniques, achieving numerous recognitions including as the [[Guggenheim Fellowship]] for Natural Sciences and [[Sloan Fellowship]]. She holds a faculty position at New York University (NYU), where she has been since 1998.

==Education==

Farrar obtained a bachelor's degree at [[UC Berkeley]] in 1968, being one of the first undergraduate students to enroll in graduate courses in the physics department. After graduating from UC Berkeley, Farrar went on to earn her PhD from [[Princeton University|Princeton]] in 1971, becoming the first woman to receive a physics PhD from Princeton.<ref name="faculty">{{cite web |url=http://as.nyu.edu/content/nyu-as/as/faculty/glennys-farrar.html |title=Glennys Farrar |website=[[New York University]] |access-date=2019-04-28 |archive-date=2019-05-16 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190516003315/http://as.nyu.edu/content/nyu-as/as/faculty/glennys-farrar.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="cuny">{{cite web|url=https://www.ccny.cuny.edu/calendar/henry-semat-lecture-physics-glennys-r-farrar-could-dark-matter-be-made-quarks |title=Henry Semat Lecture in Physics: Glennys R Farrar, Could Dark Matter be Made of Quarks? |website=[[City College of New York]] |access-date=2019-04-28}}</ref><ref name="worldsciencefestival">{{cite web |url=https://www.worldsciencefestival.com/participants/glennys_farrar/ |title=Glennys Farrar |website=[[World Science Festival]] |access-date=2019-04-28 |archive-date=2020-02-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200205005813/https://www.worldsciencefestival.com/participants/glennys_farrar/ |url-status=live }}</ref> During this time she began studying Hindi alongside her physics endeavors, culminating in an independent studies program at [[Delhi University]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=What Glennys Farrar Covets Is more hours In the day |url=http://calteches.library.caltech.edu/34/3/Farrar.htm |access-date=2022-04-25 |website=calteches.library.caltech.edu}}</ref>

==Career==
After graduating from Princeton, Farrar held post-doctoral positions at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]]<ref name="ias2">{{cite web |title=Glennys Farrar |url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/glennys-farrar |access-date=2019-04-28 |website=[[Institute for Advanced Study]]}}</ref> and [[Caltech]]. During her time at Caltech, Farrar improved the current understanding of the Pion form-factor,<ref>{{Cite web |title=INSPIRE |url=https://inspirehep.net/literature/140564 |access-date=2022-04-25 |website=inspirehep.net}}</ref> and proposed a new model for elastic [[nucleon]] scattering.<ref>{{Cite web |title=INSPIRE |url=https://inspirehep.net/literature/133219 |access-date=2022-04-25 |website=inspirehep.net}}</ref> She accepted a faculty position at [[Rutgers University]] in 1979, where her work continued to probe Standard Model interactions and contemporary developments in Supersymmetric string theory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=INSPIRE |url=https://inspirehep.net/literature/35021 |access-date=2022-04-25 |website=inspirehep.net}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=INSPIRE |url=https://inspirehep.net/literature/445344 |access-date=2022-04-25 |website=inspirehep.net}}</ref> Farrar joined the physics faculty at NYU in 1998, where she currently resides. While at NYU, she chaired the physics department and founded the Center for Cosmology and Particle Physics.<ref name="worldsciencefestival"/>

Farrar has garnered several honors for her achievements in theoretical physics. In 1975, she was awarded a [[Sloan Research Fellowship]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://sloan.org/past-fellows |title=Past Fellows |website=[[Alfred P. Sloan Foundation]] |access-date=2019-04-28 |archive-date=2018-03-14 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180314000756/https://sloan.org/past-fellows |url-status=dead }}</ref> and received a [[Guggenheim Fellowship]] in 1984.<ref>{{cite web|title=Glennys R. Farrar|url=https://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/glennys-r-farrar/|access-date=2019-04-28|website=[[John Simon Guggenheim Foundation]]}}</ref> She was elected in 2003 a Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] (AAAS).<ref>{{cite web|title=Historic Fellows|website=American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS)|url=https://www.aaas.org/fellows/historic|access-date=2023-01-05|archive-date=2019-03-27|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190327091455/https://www.aaas.org/fellows/historic|url-status=live}}</ref> In 2014 and 2021, Farrar was selected as a [[Simons Fellow]] in Theoretical Physics.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.simonsfoundation.org/grant/simons-fellows-in-theoretical-physics/?tab=awardees |website=[[Simons Foundation]] |title=Simons Fellows in Theoretical Physics |access-date=2019-04-28}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-02-04|title=2021 Simons Fellows in Mathematics and Theoretical Physics Announced|url=https://www.simonsfoundation.org/2021/02/04/2021-simons-fellows-in-mathematics-and-theoretical-physics-announced/|access-date=2021-07-18|website=Simons Foundation|language=en-US}}</ref> She was also the chair of the Division of Astrophysics (DAP) of the [[American Physical Society]] for the 2021-2022 period.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Governance - Unit - DAP |url=https://engage.aps.org/dap/governance/executive-committee/committee-members?Execute=1 |access-date=2022-04-10 |website=engage.aps.org}}</ref> She was elected to the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2023 NAS Election |url=http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2023-nas-election.html |access-date=2023-08-25 |website=www.nasonline.org |archive-date=2023-05-03 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230503155938/http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2023-nas-election.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> In 2025, Farrar joined the Simons Society of Fellows as a Senior Fellow.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-07-02 |title=Simons Society of Fellows Welcomes 3 New Senior Fellows |url=https://www.simonsfoundation.org/2025/07/02/simons-society-of-fellows-welcomes-3-new-senior-fellows/ |access-date=2026-09-19 |website=Simons Foundation |language=en-US}}</ref> As of August 2026, the Simons Foundation announced that they will be funding 12 Math and Physics research groups, one of which being on Cosmic Magnetism which Farrar is the director of. <ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-08-06 |title=Simons Foundation Funds 12 Targeted Math and Physics Research Groups |url=https://www.simonsfoundation.org/2026/08/06/simons-foundation-funds-12-targeted-math-and-physics-research-groups/ |access-date=2026-09-30 |website=Simons Foundation |language=en-US}}</ref> 

Farrar has spent many years of her career working on understanding the sources of the highest-energy comic rays. She has significantly contributed to the research<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=The Pierre Auger Collaboration |last2=Aab |first2=A. |last3=Abreu |first3=P. |last4=Aglietta |first4=M. |last5=Al Samarai |first5=I. |last6=Albuquerque |first6=I. F. M. |last7=Allekotte |first7=I. |last8=Almela |first8=A. |last9=Alvarez Castillo |first9=J. |last10=Alvarez-Muñiz |first10=J. |last11=Anastasi |first11=G. A. |date=2017-09-22 |title=Observation of a large-scale anisotropy in the arrival directions of cosmic rays above 8 × 10 18 eV |url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.aan4338 |journal=Science |language=en |volume=357 |issue=6357 |pages=1266–1270 |doi=10.1126/science.aan4338 |pmid=28935800 |arxiv=1709.07321 |bibcode=2017Sci...357.1266P |s2cid=3679232 |issn=0036-8075}}</ref> conducted by the [[Pierre Auger Observatory]], with more than one-hundred publications<ref>{{Cite web |title=INSPIRE |url=https://inspirehep.net/authors/1010333 |access-date=2022-04-10 |website=inspirehep.net}}</ref> in this experiment alone. As a theoretical physicist she has worked on developing tools for particle-detection from high energy sources in the universe. In 2012, Ronnie Jansson (then a graduate student) and Farrar, published an article presenting a new model of the galactic magnetic field.<ref>{{Cite journal |url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/0004-637X/757/1/14/meta |language=en |doi=10.1088/0004-637x/757/1/14|title=A New Model of the Galactic Magnetic Field |year=2012 |last1=Jansson |first1=Ronnie |last2=Farrar |first2=Glennys R. |journal=The Astrophysical Journal |volume=757 |issue=1 |page=14 |arxiv=1204.3662 |bibcode=2012ApJ...757...14J |s2cid=46502748 }}</ref>
